# Tandem Rolling Equipment System for LED Bond-Packaging with Organic Silicone Resin Photoconverters

## System Overview

The equipment system employs a tandem rolling process to bond-package light-emitting diodes (LEDs) with an organic silicone resin photoconverter. The system is composed of two primary components: a protective film removing apparatus and a roll-bonding apparatus. Together, these units enable an integrated, streamlined approach to the packaging of LED devices.

## Protective Film Removing Apparatus

The protective film removing apparatus is designed to prepare the photoconversion sheet for the subsequent bonding process. It consists of several sequentially connected stages that work in coordination. First, a photoconversion sheet freezing part cools the sheet to the appropriate temperature, facilitating the clean separation of the protective layer. Next, a traction part pulls off the single-side protective film from the sheet. Finally, a sheet rewarming part restores the photoconversion sheet to a suitable working temperature, preparing it for the bonding stage. This sequential arrangement ensures efficient and reliable removal of the protective film without damaging the delicate photoconversion material.

## Roll-Bonding Apparatus

The roll-bonding apparatus is responsible for packaging the LED array with the prepared photoconversion sheet. It utilizes two single-wheeled rollers, both of which feature smooth rolling surfaces. These rollers work together to package a flip chip LED array using the single-side protective film sheet. The smooth surfaces of the rollers ensure uniform pressure distribution and a consistent bond between the photoconversion sheet and the LED array, resulting in high-quality packaging.

## Key Advantages

The principal advantage of this equipment system lies in its ability to enable a continuous rolling process for the bond-packaging of LEDs with organic silicone resin photoconverters. By integrating the protective film removal and roll-bonding operations into a coordinated, tandem workflow, the system eliminates interruptions that would otherwise arise from handling these steps separately.

## Industrial Application and Benefits

This invention offers significant benefits for industrialized batch production of LED packages. By streamlining the packaging process and ensuring consistent, high-quality bonding, the system substantially improves both the production efficiency and the yield of LED packages. As a result, it represents a valuable advancement for manufacturers seeking to scale up LED production while maintaining reliable product quality.

# LED Bond-Packaging Equipment System Using Organic Silicone Resin Photoconverter

## Overview

This equipment system provides an integrated solution for the bond-packaging of LED devices, utilizing an organic silicone resin photoconverter applied through a tandem rolling process. The system is specifically designed to package flip chip LED arrays with high precision and efficiency, addressing the growing demands of industrialized LED production.

## System Architecture

The equipment system comprises two principal apparatus working in tandem: a protective film removing apparatus and a roll-bonding apparatus. These components operate sequentially to achieve a continuous, streamlined packaging workflow.

### Protective Film Removing Apparatus

The protective film removing apparatus is responsible for the careful separation of protective films from the organic silicone resin photoconverter prior to bonding. This apparatus incorporates three functional sections:

- **Freezing Part:** This section lowers the temperature of the protective film and adjacent materials, altering their physical properties to facilitate clean separation. The freezing process reduces adhesion characteristics and prevents damage to the delicate photoconverter layer during removal.

- **Traction Part:** Following the freezing stage, the traction mechanism applies controlled pulling force to peel away the protective film. The precise tension management ensures that the film is removed smoothly without tearing or leaving residue on the photoconverter surface.

- **Rewarming Part:** After film removal, the rewarming section restores the material to an appropriate working temperature, conditioning the organic silicone resin photoconverter for the subsequent bonding operation and ensuring optimal material behavior during roll-bonding.

### Roll-Bonding Apparatus

The roll-bonding apparatus employs smooth single-wheeled rollers to bond the prepared organic silicone resin photoconverter onto the flip chip LED arrays. The smooth surface of the single-wheeled roller design ensures uniform pressure distribution across the packaging surface, promoting consistent bonding quality and eliminating defects such as air entrapment, uneven adhesion, or surface irregularities.

## Process Advantages

By integrating these apparatus into a tandem rolling configuration, the system enables a fully continuous rolling process. This continuous operation satisfies the specific technical requirements for organic silicone resin photoconverter packaging, maintaining the material integrity and optical performance essential for high-quality LED devices.

## Industrial Benefits

The continuous, automated nature of this equipment system delivers substantial advantages for large-scale manufacturing. By streamlining the film removal and bonding operations into a seamless workflow, the system significantly improves production efficiency and enhances yield rates. These benefits make the equipment particularly well-suited for industrialized batch production of LED packages, supporting cost-effective, high-throughput manufacturing while maintaining rigorous quality standards.

# The Evolution of LED Technology

The light-emitting diode, commonly known as the LED, has transformed the way we illuminate our world. Since its early development in the twentieth century, this remarkable technology has grown from a simple indicator light into one of the most efficient and versatile lighting solutions available today.

## What Is an LED?

The LED is a semiconductor device that emits light when an electric current passes through it. Unlike traditional incandescent bulbs, which produce light by heating a filament, the LED generates illumination through a process called electroluminescence. This fundamental difference is what makes the LED so much more energy-efficient than older lighting technologies.

## The Advantages

The benefits of LED technology are numerous and significant:

- **Energy efficiency**: The LED uses up to 80% less energy than incandescent bulbs, making it a cost-effective choice for homes and businesses.
- **Longevity**: A typical LED can last tens of thousands of hours, far outlasting conventional light sources.
- **Durability**: Because the LED contains no fragile filaments, it is highly resistant to shocks and vibrations.
- **Environmental impact**: The LED contains no harmful mercury and produces less waste over its lifetime.

## Modern Applications

Today, the LED can be found nearly everywhere. From the screens of our smartphones and televisions to the headlights of our cars, this technology has become deeply integrated into daily life. The LED also plays a vital role in street lighting, medical devices, and even agricultural systems, where specialized LEDs help plants grow indoors.

## Looking Ahead

As research continues, the future of the LED looks bright. Engineers are constantly finding new ways to improve efficiency, color quality, and affordability. The LED will undoubtedly remain at the forefront of lighting innovation for years to come, lighting the path toward a more sustainable and energy-conscious world.

# Patent Abstract

## Equipment System for Bond-Packaging LEDs Using Tandem Rolling with Organic Silicone Resin Photoconverter

**Abstract**

An equipment system is disclosed for bond-packaging light-emitting diodes (LEDs) with an organic silicone resin photoconverter layer using a tandem rolling process. The system comprises a protective film removing apparatus and a roll-bonding apparatus arranged in tandem to enable continuous, automated fabrication of phosphor-converted LED packages.

The protective film removing apparatus includes a feed mechanism configured to advance a laminated photoconverter sheet comprising an organic silicone resin layer containing dispersed wavelength-conversion phosphor material, the silicone resin layer being covered on at least one surface by a releasable protective film. The apparatus further comprises a peeling member and a take-up roller that engage and separate the protective film from the silicone resin photoconverter layer, together with a tension-control assembly that maintains dimensional stability of the exposed resin layer during film removal.

The roll-bonding apparatus is positioned downstream of the protective film removing apparatus and includes a pair of opposed rollers defining a nip through which an LED-bearing substrate and the exposed organic silicone resin photoconverter layer are conveyed in registration. The rollers apply controlled compressive pressure and, in certain embodiments, elevated temperature to laminate and bond the photoconverter layer onto the light-emitting surfaces of the LEDs. A heating unit may be incorporated to partially or fully cure the silicone resin during or after bonding.

By integrating the protective film removing apparatus and the roll-bonding apparatus in a tandem configuration, the system achieves continuous in-line processing, uniform photoconverter layer thickness across multiple LED devices, reduced void formation at the bonding interface, and improved throughput and color-conversion consistency in the manufacture of packaged LEDs.

---

# Technical Summary: LED Packaging System with Thermal-Assisted Film Removal and Roller Bonding

## System Overview

This LED packaging system automates the application of a photoconversion sheet (e.g., phosphor or quantum-dot conversion layer) onto a flip chip LED array. The system's distinguishing feature is a multi-stage thermal process for removing protective films from the photoconversion sheet, followed by a controlled roller-bonding operation that adheres the conversion layer to the LED array.

## Key Functional Stages

### 1. Freezing Stage
The photoconversion sheet, delivered with protective films laminated to one or both surfaces, first enters a **freezing/cooling module**. Lowering the sheet and film assembly to a controlled sub-ambient temperature alters the adhesion characteristics at the film–sheet interface:

- Reduces tackiness of the adhesive bonding the protective film
- Induces differential thermal contraction between the film and the conversion sheet
- Embrittles the interface to promote clean, residue-free separation

This thermal conditioning prevents tearing or stretching of the delicate photoconversion layer during subsequent removal.

### 2. Traction (Peeling) Stage
Following freezing, a **traction mechanism** applies controlled mechanical force to separate the protective film from the conversion sheet:

- Grippers or take-up rollers engage the film's leading edge
- Peel angle and tension are regulated to exploit the weakened, cold interface
- The reduced adhesion achieved in the freezing stage allows the film to release cleanly without transferring adhesive residue or deforming the sheet

### 3. Rewarming Stage
After film removal, the exposed photoconversion sheet passes through a **rewarming module** that returns it to a suitable bonding temperature:

- Restores sheet pliability and dimensional stability
- Prepares the exposed adhesive/conversion surface for optimal bonding
- Eliminates condensation risk that could compromise the bond interface

## Roller Bonding of Conversion Sheet to LED Array

Once conditioned, the photoconversion sheet is bonded to the flip chip LED array using a **smooth-surfaced roller assembly**:

- The smooth roller surface distributes bonding pressure uniformly across the sheet
- Progressive line-contact rolling expels trapped air and prevents void or bubble formation
- Uniform pressure ensures consistent optical coupling and bond-line thickness across all LED emitters
- The smooth finish avoids imprinting surface texture or defects onto the optically active conversion layer

Because flip chip LEDs present their emitting surface upward (with electrical contacts on the underside), the conversion sheet can be laminated directly across the array's top surface without interference from wire bonds, enabling a planar, high-uniformity bonding process.

## Advantages

| Feature | Benefit |
|---------|---------|
| Thermal-assisted film removal | Clean separation without residue or sheet damage |
| Freeze–peel–rewarm sequence | Preserves delicate conversion layer integrity |
| Smooth-roller bonding | Void-free, uniform optical bond line |
| Flip chip compatibility | Planar lamination without wire-bond obstruction |

## Summary

The system integrates thermal management and mechanical precision to achieve reliable photoconversion sheet application. By using freezing to weaken film adhesion, controlled traction for clean peeling, and rewarming for bonding readiness—followed by smooth-roller lamination—the process yields consistent, high-quality color-converted LED packages with minimized defects and improved optical uniformity.

# LED Bond-Packaging Equipment System

## Formal Patent-Style Description

An LED bond-packaging equipment system comprising a film-removal mechanism and a roll-bonding assembly configured to process a double-sided protective photoconversion sheet, wherein said system operates as follows: A double-sided protective photoconversion sheet, comprising a central photoconversion layer bounded on opposing surfaces by a first protective film and a second protective film, is advanced along a conveyance path by a transport means toward a peeling station. At said peeling station, a film-removal mechanism engages an edge portion of the first protective film disposed on a lower or designated surface of the photoconversion sheet, whereupon a peeling member—which may comprise a peeling blade, a peeling roller, or a peeling belt oriented at a predetermined acute angle relative to the sheet plane—separates said first protective film from the photoconversion layer by directing the removed film along a divergent path while the photoconversion layer, together with the retained second protective film, continues along the primary conveyance path. The removed first protective film is thereafter directed toward and collected upon a waste-recovery reel or equivalent take-up means. Subsequent to said film-removal step, the photoconversion sheet, now bearing an exposed adhesive or bonding surface where the first protective film was removed, is conveyed to a roll-bonding station comprising at least one bonding roller, wherein the exposed surface of the photoconversion sheet is brought into registered alignment with a target substrate bearing one or more LED elements. The bonding roller thereupon applies a controlled compressive force, and optionally a regulated thermal input, across the interface between the exposed surface of the photoconversion sheet and the LED-bearing substrate as the roller traverses the bonding region, thereby effecting a uniform and substantially void-free adhesion of the photoconversion sheet to said substrate, whereby the retained second protective film continues to shield the opposing surface of the photoconversion layer throughout the bonding operation and may be removed in a subsequent processing stage.

---
